analysisSummary: MECHANISM CONFIRMED AS CODE FACT (quotes re-verified at pinned HEAD 9007ba1352e606575e32456512e25c41a9bf449c, tree clean): Nexus.sol:306-334 initializeAccount wraps ALL guards in `if (msg.sender != address(this))`, so a self-call skips the transient-flag check (Initializable.requireInitializable, else-branch), the 7702 relay signature + !isInitialized() + replay checks (lines 314-328), and any !isInitialized() check, then unconditionally runs _initializeAccount (line 333). _initializeAccount (336-356) parses a caller-supplied bootstrap address + bootstrapCall from initData and runs bootstrap.delegatecall(bootstrapCall) (line 350) with no allowlist; the post-check require(isInitialized()) (353-355) passes trivially on an already-initialized non-7702 account and is skipped for 7702 accounts. Commit 0b64d29 verified via git show: it added ONLY the relay-branch !isInitialized() require. The self branch is by design for 7702 first-init (natspec Nexus.sol:304-305). REACHABILITY — every path to msg.sender == address(this) on an initialized account traced independently: (a) EntryPoint userOp -> execute() (Nexus.sol:144, onlyEntryPoint + withHook) with CALLTYPE_SINGLE/BATCH target == address(this): _handleSingleExecution (ExecutionHelper.sol:205-213) decodes an arbitrary target, no denylist (grep confirms none), and _execute (ExecutionHelper.sol:39-56) uses a raw CALL, so the self-call arrives with msg.sender == address(this). But the userOp must first pass validateUserOp (Nexus.sol:102-138); _handleValidator (ModuleManager.sol:637-644) resolves address(0) to the default validator and otherwise requires the validator be installed. The ONLY module shipping in-repo is K1Validator (contracts/modules/ contains only validators/K1Validator.sol; no session/policy validator, executor, or hook in-repo; SCOPE.md confirms session modules live outside this repo and out of bounty scope), and K1Validator.validateUserOp (K1Validator.sol:147-149) checks ONLY an owner ECDSA signature with NO callData/policy inspection. So this path requires the OWNER'S OWN KEY: self-action, not attacker use. (b) executeFromExecutor() (Nexus.sol:162-170, onlyExecutorModule + withHook + withRegistry): executors are owner-installed via owner-gated installModule (Nexus.sol:226, onlyEntryPointOrSelf) and fully trusted. (c) Direct 7702 EOA self-transaction: only the EOA key holder can originate a tx with msg.sender == the EOA (ECDSA tx authentication; _amIERC7702 detection ModuleManager.sol:624-635); owner-only self-action, the same key the relay branch trusts. (d) Nested calls: NO new path — hooks, fallback handlers, and validators are CALLED BY the account, so callbacks have msg.sender == module address and hit the guarded branch; the only other account-originated self-CALL is _enableMode's this.installModule (ModuleManager.sol:174) with a FIXED selector; executeUserOp (Nexus.sol:190-196) uses address(this).delegatecall, which preserves msg.sender == EntryPoint, so initializeAccount reached that way hits the GUARDED branch; executeComposable (Nexus.sol:201-203, onlyEntryPoint + withHook -> _executeAction -> _executeMemory CALL) admits the same EntryPoint-validated principal as execute(). (e) Factory: NexusProxy constructor calls setInitializable() then upgradeToAndCall via DELEGATECALL, so msg.sender is the deployer, not address(this); the transient-flag branch applies and requireInitializable() (Initializable.sol:30-39) CONSUMES the flag, single-use per deploying transaction. ZERO INCREMENTAL PRIVILEGE for every reachable principal: the same principal, through the SAME outer validation and SAME outer withHook, can already (1) run CALLTYPE_DELEGATECALL via execute()/executeFromExecutor() (Nexus.sol:144-157, 162-185; ExecutionHelper.sol:227-237 -> 151-168 _executeDelegatecall, no target restriction) — arbitrary code in account storage context, the IDENTICAL primitive to the bootstrap delegatecall and a strict superset (any bootstrapCall is expressible as a delegatecall payload; delegatecalled code can SSTORE any slot directly, so a custom bootstrap is NOT strictly more powerful than delegatecall-mode execute); (2) for proxy accounts, execute a self-call to upgradeToAndCall (Nexus.sol:462; _authorizeUpgrade Nexus.sol:511-516 onlyEntryPointOrSelf, satisfied by self-call; blocked only for 7702) replacing the implementation entirely; (3) execute a self-call to installModule (Nexus.sol:226) installing an arbitrary module. Hook/registry bypass sub-claim OVERSTATED: the outer execute()/executeFromExecutor() DO carry withHook (Nexus.sol:144, 169), so the transaction IS hook-checked at the outer level; the stock NexusBootstrap path ALSO runs withHook+withRegistry because NexusBootstrap is ModuleManager (NexusBootstrap.sol:51) and its _init* functions call _configureRegistry FIRST then _installValidator/_installExecutor/_installHook/_installFallbackHandler/_installPreValidationHook (NexusBootstrap.sol:159-191, 247-248, 322-353, 413-423), each carrying withHook+withRegistry (ModuleManager.sol:222-223, 256-257, 282-283, 320-321, 375-376); only a CUSTOM bootstrap skips the inner checks — exactly as delegatecall-mode execute does; and withRegistry NO-OPS when no registry is configured (RegistryAdapter.sol:46-51, opt-in). The finding therefore requires a hypothetical validator policy permitting a self-targeted initializeAccount call while FORBIDDING the strictly-equivalent delegatecall-mode execute, installModule self-call, and upgradeToAndCall self-call. No such validator exists in-repo, no evidence supports such a policy shape, and session modules are out of bounty scope. RUBRIC/GATE: Hunter High ('authenticated privilege escalation') FAILS — no privilege escalation occurs because no principal gains any capability it lacks. Triage pre-severity gate: only a middle primitive is confirmed, no full chain to attacker-attainable impact; attacker walks away with NOTHING (needs the owner key, with which the account is already theirs); validation (validateUserOp owner signature / owner-gated executor install) still gates the chain; Q1 (attacker use right now) = NO, Q4 (requires unobtainable privilege) = YES. Hunter's own concession ('a pure owner-key account gains nothing beyond the owner's existing power') is correct and fatal. DEDUP (checked myself, root-cause basis): NOT EX-116 (GHSA stale transient flag: classic-path SECOND call in the deploying transaction passing an uncleared flag — different guard, different trigger; the self branch never consults the flag, so distinct mechanism; distinctness does not save the finding, which fails on impact); NOT EX-049 (Zenith L-1: default validator VALIDATING without isInitialized() — validation gating, not re-init); NOT EX-I20 (Cantina 5.5.20: initializeAccount never verifying a validator was installed — the post-check observation; different root cause: missing installed-validator check vs missing !isInitialized() guard on the self branch); PARTIAL EFFECT OVERLAP ONLY with EX-067 (Pashov L-12, hook bypass via NexusBootstrap lacking withHook — different mechanism) and EX-073/EX-074 (session-key oracle-confusion escape via enable-mode/emergency-uninstall — different mechanism); neither is a root-cause duplicate. Verdict rests on reachability/impact, not dedup. The missing !isInitialized() check on the self branch is a genuine hardening gap (it would not break the intended 7702 first-init flow, where the account is uninitialized), but as a High-severity bounty finding it is NOT_A_BUG: verified mechanism, no attacker use, zero incremental impact.
suggestedFix: Add an unconditional require(!isInitialized(), AccountAlreadyInitialized()) at the top of Nexus.initializeAccount (or inside the msg.sender == address(this) branch) before _initializeAccount runs, so an already-initialized account can never be re-initialized through the self-call path. This does not break the intended 7702 first-init flow (the account is uninitialized at that point, per the Nexus.sol:304-305 natspec), the factory path (uninitialized at deployment), or the PREP path (validateUserOp PREP branch calls the internal _initializeAccount directly after its own !isInitialized() check at Nexus.sol:129, and is unaffected by a guard on the external initializeAccount).
